newsitem.title: USA: Document says Swiss sent vital exports to Nazis.
newsitem.headline: Document says Swiss sent vital exports to Nazis.

text.p: After Switzerland stopped supplying Germany with weapons in 1944, it continued aiding the Nazis with vital exports and electric power, according to a Second World War document released on Wednesday by the World Jewish Congress.

The WJC released the document, a plea by a U.S. official for an embargo on French exports to Switzerland, after a Swiss historian said his country's archives showed that two-thirds of Swiss munitions exports went to Germany during the war.
Swiss historian Mauro Cerutti said Nazi Germany got nearly two-thirds of Swiss exports of arms and war material from 1940 to 1944. It received arms worth $422 million at the time.

The new documents come on the heels of a scathing U.S. government report published earlier this month that alleged the Swiss were bankers to the Nazis and Switzerland's commerce with Nazi Germany, including trade in looted gold, helped to prolong the war.

The WJC document, found in the U.S. National Archive, said that after the Swiss agreed to eliminate direct munition exports to Germany, they sent that country millions of dollars worth of material that could have aided the German war effort.

This material included machine tools, precision instruments, watchmaker tools, chronometers, gas motors, cars, tractors, dynamos, steam machines and hydraulic motors. They also sent industrial chemicals, textiles and aluminum to Germany and allowed their country's railroads to ship goods from Italy to Germany.
The October 1944 document released by the WJC was written by Undersecretary of War Robert Patterson to the War Department's general staff.
In it, Patterson said, "In my opinion, Switzerland should not be permitted to make imports across France until she has completely stopped all the war aid she is rendering to Germany."
